mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate directly reduces the risk-free rate, increasing the present value of future equity cash flows and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 2.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% signals a tight labor market, boosting consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE is below 3.5%, SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which accelerates corporate revenue growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint increase in HOUST and RSAFS fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: In a manufacturing expansion regime (INDPRO above 110), rising industrial production signals robust economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO is above 110, SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A CPI reading above 2.5% annualized inflation rate signals persistent inflation, prompting the Fed to tighten policy, which negatively impacts equity valuations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL YoY growth is above 2.5%, SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a strengthening labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS is rising.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate declines and CPI rises above 2.5%, the market interprets this as a dovish Fed response to inflation, reducing real rates and supporting equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition of FEDFUNDS decline and CPI above 2.5% fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate above 2.0% signals robust economic expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When GDPC1 growth rate is above 2.0%, SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of cases.
